title: Indian History Test 2 (Modern India & Freedom Struggle — most probable)

questions.q: The Battle of Plassey (1757), which began British rule in India, was fought between Robert Clive and:
questions.explain: Clive defeated the Nawab of Bengal, Siraj-ud-Daulah, at Plassey (Palashi) in present-day West Bengal.

questions.q: The Battle of Buxar was fought in:
questions.explain: After Buxar (1764), the East India Company got the Diwani (revenue rights) of Bengal, Bihar and Odisha.

questions.q: The first British law to regulate the East India Company was the:
questions.explain: The Regulating Act 1773 was Parliament's first step to control the Company; it created the Governor-General of Bengal.

questions.q: The Revolt of 1857 began on 10 May 1857 at:
questions.explain: Sepoys at Meerut rose on 10 May 1857 and marched to Delhi the next day.

questions.q: Mangal Pandey, whose action sparked early unrest in 1857, was a sepoy at:
questions.explain: Mangal Pandey attacked British officers at Barrackpore (near Kolkata) in March 1857 over the greased cartridges.

questions.q: During the Revolt of 1857, the Mughal emperor proclaimed as the leader of the revolt was:
questions.explain: The aged Bahadur Shah Zafar was declared Emperor of India by the rebels in Delhi.

questions.q: Rani Lakshmibai, the heroine of 1857, fought the British at:
questions.explain: The Rani of Jhansi died fighting near Gwalior in 1858 and is the most remembered woman leader of the revolt.

questions.q: Kunwar Singh, the elderly zamindar who led the 1857 revolt, belonged to:
questions.explain: Kunwar Singh of Jagdishpur (Arrah, Bihar) fought the British at the age of about 80.

questions.q: Begum Hazrat Mahal led the Revolt of 1857 in:
questions.explain: Begum Hazrat Mahal ruled Awadh in the name of her son Birjis Qadr during the revolt.

questions.q: After the Revolt of 1857, the rule of India passed to the British Crown by the:
questions.explain: The Act of 1858 ended Company rule; the Queen's Proclamation followed, and the Viceroy replaced the Governor-General.

questions.q: The Indian National Congress was founded in:
questions.explain: The Indian National Congress (INC) was founded in December 1885 with A.O. Hume's initiative.

questions.q: The first President of the Indian National Congress was:
questions.explain: Womesh Chunder Bonnerjee presided over the first session; Hume was the founder-secretary, not president — a classic trap.

questions.q: The first session of the Indian National Congress (1885) was held at:
questions.explain: The first session met in Bombay with 72 delegates; it was originally planned at Poona.

questions.q: The Partition of Bengal (1905) was carried out by:
questions.explain: Curzon divided Bengal, officially for administration; Indians saw it as divide and rule.

questions.q: The movement launched in response to the Partition of Bengal was the:
questions.explain: Swadeshi (use Indian goods, boycott foreign goods) was the direct answer to Bengal's partition; the partition was annulled in 1911.

questions.q: The Muslim League was founded in 1906 at:
questions.explain: The All-India Muslim League was founded in Dhaka in December 1906.

questions.q: The Lucknow Pact of 1916 is known for:
questions.explain: At Lucknow, Congress and the Muslim League made a joint scheme, and the two Congress factions (Moderates and Extremists) reunited.

questions.q: Mahatma Gandhi returned to India from South Africa in:
questions.explain: Gandhi returned on 9 January 1915 — the day now marked as Pravasi Bharatiya Divas.

questions.q: Gandhi's first Satyagraha in India (1917) was at:
questions.explain: At Champaran (Bihar) Gandhi fought for indigo farmers forced to grow indigo under the tinkathia system.

questions.q: The Jallianwala Bagh massacre took place on:
questions.explain: On Baisakhi day, 13 April 1919, General Dyer's troops fired on an unarmed crowd in Amritsar.

questions.q: The officer responsible for the Jallianwala Bagh firing was:
questions.explain: Brigadier-General R.E.H. Dyer ordered the firing; the massacre shocked India and weakened faith in British rule.

questions.q: The Non-Cooperation Movement was launched by Gandhi in:
questions.explain: Launched in August 1920 against the Rowlatt Act, Jallianwala Bagh and the Khilafat wrongs.

questions.q: Gandhi withdrew the Non-Cooperation Movement in 1922 because of:
questions.explain: At Chauri Chaura (UP), a mob killed 22 policemen; Gandhi, committed to non-violence, called off the movement.

questions.q: The Simon Commission (1928) was boycotted because:
questions.explain: All seven members were British; Indians protested with 'Simon Go Back' across the country.

questions.q: Lala Lajpat Rai died in 1928 from injuries received during a protest against:
questions.explain: He was lathi-charged during the Lahore protest against Simon Commission and died shortly after.

questions.q: The Dandi March of 1930 was undertaken to break the:
questions.explain: Gandhi walked from Sabarmati to Dandi (12 March–6 April 1930) and made salt, starting the Civil Disobedience Movement.

questions.q: The movement that began with the Dandi March was the:
questions.explain: Civil Disobedience (1930-34) meant deliberately breaking unjust laws, beginning with the salt law.

questions.q: The Gandhi-Irwin Pact was signed in:
questions.explain: Under the 1931 pact Gandhi suspended Civil Disobedience and agreed to attend the Second Round Table Conference.

questions.q: The Poona Pact (1932) was an agreement between Gandhi and:
questions.explain: The Poona Pact replaced separate electorates for Depressed Classes with reserved seats in joint electorates.

questions.q: The Quit India Movement was launched in:
questions.explain: Launched on 8 August 1942 at Bombay with Gandhi's call of 'Do or Die'.

questions.q: The slogan 'Do or Die' (Karo Ya Maro) is associated with:
questions.explain: Gandhi gave this mantra during the Quit India Movement of 1942.

questions.q: The Indian National Army (Azad Hind Fauj) was led by:
questions.explain: Bose took command of the Indian National Army (INA) in 1943 in Singapore and gave the call 'Delhi Chalo' and 'Jai Hind'.

questions.q: The Forward Bloc party was founded in 1939 by:
questions.explain: After resigning as Congress President in 1939, Bose formed the Forward Bloc.

questions.q: Bhagat Singh, Rajguru and Sukhdev were hanged on:
questions.explain: They were executed in Lahore jail for the Saunders murder case; 23 March is observed as Shaheed Diwas.

questions.q: The Cabinet Mission, which proposed a plan for India's future constitution, came in:
questions.explain: The Cabinet Mission (1946) proposed a federal union and grouping of provinces; it set the path to the Constituent Assembly.

questions.q: The last Viceroy of British India was:
questions.explain: Mountbatten, the last Viceroy, also became the first Governor-General of independent India.

questions.q: The first Indian Governor-General of independent India was:
questions.explain: Rajaji took over from Mountbatten in June 1948 and was the only Indian to hold the post.

questions.q: India became independent on 15 August 1947 under the:
questions.explain: The British Parliament's Independence Act created the two dominions of India and Pakistan.

questions.q: Shivaji, the founder of the Maratha kingdom, was crowned (coronation) in 1674 at:
questions.explain: Shivaji was crowned Chhatrapati at Raigad fort in 1674; he was famous for guerrilla warfare in the Sahyadris.

questions.q: The Third Battle of Panipat (1761) was fought between the Marathas and:
questions.explain: Abdali (Durrani) defeated the Marathas in 1761, a turning point that weakened Maratha power in the north.
